review.tagline: Coding agent for terminal, desktop, browser and VS Code, with DeepSeek preset
review.summary: Reasonix is a Go coding agent that reads a project folder, edits files and runs commands and tests, showing each step. Models are set in reasonix.toml: a DeepSeek preset is built in and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint is a config entry. It ships as the Studio desktop app, a CLI/TUI, a local web UI (`reasonix web`), and a VS Code extension or ACP connection for other editors.
review.audience: Developers wanting a self-run coding agent with a choice of model provider
strengths: Any OpenAI-compatible provider is a config entry; DeepSeek ships as a preset
Permission levels and plan mode; forbid rules always apply
Rewind by conversation turn without touching git history
Static single binary (CGO_ENABLED=0), cross-compiled to six targets
weaknesses: Rewind covers only files its edit tools changed, not shell command effects
2.x line is still moving quickly; 1.x is the stable branch
VS Code extension requires installing the 1.x CLI separately
Model provider receives what the agent reads; no local model setup documented
needs: Needs Model provider API key, Go 1.25+ (build from source), Node 24+ and pnpm 10 (build Studio)
Models: DeepSeek, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, MCP servers
